dossier.purpose: GPT Researcher is an open-source Python library and FastAPI/WebSocket service (plus static and NextJS frontends, a repo-root CLI, LangGraph and AG2 multi-agent examples, and a LangChain 'deepagents' example) that takes a query, has an LLM plan sub-queries, retrieves and scrapes web pages or local documents (optionally through MCP tools), filters the context, and has an LLM write a markdown report with in-text hyperlink citations and a reference list (README.md:25-27; gpt_researcher/agent.py:37-51,343-504). It is a research/report generator, not a general task worker: this tree contains no code-writing or code-executing agent, no sandbox, no checkpointed or resumable run state, and no OpenAI Agents SDK / Claude Agent SDK / Codex SDK integration; the only agent-harness integrations are LangGraph, AG2 and LangChain deepagents (multi_agents/, deep_agents/agent.py:6-7). LLMs are reached through LangChain chat-model classes chosen by a 'provider:model' string (27 provider names including openai and anthropic; gpt_researcher/llm_provider/generic/base.py:13-41,146-164); defaults are OpenAI gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.4-mini and Tavily search (gpt_researcher/config/variables/default.py:4-10). The repo also ships first-party benchmark artifacts (deep_agents/benchmark_results/, evals/).

claims.claim: "GPT Researcher the first open deep research agent designed for both web and local research on any given task."

"The agent produces detailed, factual, and unbiased research reports with citations"; offers customization for tailor-made, domain-specific research agents; parallelized agent work for speed and reliability.

Planner/execution/publisher architecture: the planner generates research questions, execution agents gather information (a crawler agent per question; summarize and source-track each resource), and the publisher aggregates a final report.

Feature list: reports from web and local documents; "Generate detailed reports exceeding 2,000 words"; "Aggregate over 20 sources for objective conclusions"; JavaScript-enabled scraping; "Maintains memory and context throughout research"; export to PDF/Word.
Claude Skill: `npx skills add assafelovic/gpt-researcher`; "Once installed, Claude can leverage GPT Researcher's deep research capabilities directly within your conversations."

Setup: Python 3.12 or later; git clone; export OPENAI_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY (or .env); optional OPENAI_BASE_URL for OpenAI-compatible APIs; `pip install -r requirements.txt` then `python -m uvicorn main:app --reload`; UI at http://localhost:8000.
PyPI package: `pip install gpt-researcher`; `GPTResearcher(query=...)`, then `await researcher.conduct_research()` and `await researcher.write_report()`.
MCP: GPT Researcher is an MCP client (`RETRIEVER=tavily,mcp`, `mcp_configs=[...]`) for GitHub, databases and custom APIs; the MCP server was moved to the separate repo assafelovic/gptr-mcp.

Deep Research: recursive tree-like exploration with configurable depth and breadth, concurrent processing, smart context management; "Takes ~5 minutes per deep research"; "Costs ~$0.4 per research (using `o3-mini` on "high" reasoning effort)".

Context filtering: Jev (TypeSafe; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) is the default when a key is set; otherwise, or if a Jev call fails, local keyword (BM25) ranking; on 28 research tasks 73% relevant passages (Jev) vs 51% (keyword) vs 46% (embeddings); Jev 15 wins / 10 ties / 3 losses vs embeddings.
Docker: `docker-compose up --build` starts the Python server on localhost:8000 and the React app on localhost:3000.
Local-document research via DOC_PATH for PDF, plain text, CSV, Excel, Markdown, PowerPoint and Word; `report_source` 'local' in the pip package.
Multi-agent assistant built with LangGraph and AG2 (5-6 page reports in PDF/Docx/Markdown); optional LangSmith tracing via LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2 / LANGCHAIN_API_KEY.
Disclaimer: experimental application provided "as-is" under the Apache 2 license; "NOT a recommendation to use in academic or research papers"; "We do not aim to eliminate biases".

readme.telemetry_and_network: No project-owned telemetry or phone-home found in the Python code (searched for posthog/sentry/mixpanel/analytics etc.). Opt-in tracing only: LangSmith when LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2/LANGCHAIN_API_KEY are set (README.md:313-324; .env.example:54-60), and multi_agents/main.py:42-44 and deep_agents/main.py:12-13 switch tracing on automatically whenever LANGCHAIN_API_KEY is present; `langsmith` is a hard dependency (pyproject.toml:97). Optional Monocle tracing (extra `monocle`) with exporters file/console/okahu/s3/blob/gcs (multi_agents/main.py:12-35; .env.example:62-66; pyproject.toml:205-210). The optional NextJS frontend renders next-plausible PlausibleProvider (domain localhost:3000) and @next/third-parties GoogleAnalytics with NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID in the page head (frontend/nextjs/app/layout.tsx:3-4,65-66; docker-compose.yml:33); the effect of those two libraries (third-party analytics scripts) is library behavior not visible in this tree; a trackResearchQuery hook that would send query text to GA exists but is never called (frontend/nextjs/hooks/useAnalytics.ts:22-32; components/Task/ResearchForm.tsx:26). Required network services/accounts: an LLM API (default OpenAI gpt-5.4 family, OPENAI_API_KEY; config/variables/default.py:8-10) and a search API (default Tavily, POST https://api.tavily.com/search with TAVILY_API_KEY; retrievers/tavily/tavily_search.py:40,47-62; .env.example:1-2); research also fetches arbitrary web pages, with an SSRF guard that rejects non-http(s) and private/loopback/link-local/metadata addresses unless ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true (utils/url_security.py:35-116; scraper/scraper.py:203; .env.example:87-92). An embeddings provider is needed only when CONTEXT_FILTER=embeddings (context/select.py:86-97). Optional third party: when TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set, the default 'auto' filter POSTs each ~1,000-character scraped chunk plus the research question to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (context/jev_filter.py:32,84-101,144; context/select.py:44-46); without a key nothing is sent and local keyword ranking runs (context/select.py:99-101). tiktoken downloads its BPE tables over the network on first use (.github/workflows/tests.yml:110-115; utils/costs.py:93,330-336). Missing LLM-provider packages and the tavily_extract/firecrawl scraper packages are pip-installed at runtime (llm_provider/generic/base.py:407-425; scraper/scraper.py:160-192). Backend CORS defaults allow http://localhost:3000, http://127.0.0.1:3000 and https://app.gptr.dev with credentials (backend/server/app.py:99-120). No account with the project itself is required.

entry_points.what: ASGI entry (`main:app` imports backend.server.app) and `python main.py` uvicorn launcher on 0.0.0.0:8000 (main.py:31-37); used by the README and the Dockerfile CMD (Dockerfile:64).
FastAPI app: REST (/report/, /api/reports, /api/chat, /files, /upload), WebSocket /ws, agent-discovery document; no authentication (app.py:97,371-419; Procfile:1 runs backend.server.app:app).
Repo-root argparse CLI `python cli.py "<query>" --report_type ...` writing markdown/PDF/DOCX to ./outputs (cli.py:4-8,359-362); not a packaged console script.
Library entry `from gpt_researcher import GPTResearcher` (gpt_researcher/__init__.py:1-3): async conduct_research()/write_report()/quick_search().
LangGraph multi-agent runner (ChiefEditorAgent) driven by multi_agents/task.json; langgraph.json:7 exposes multi_agents/agent.py:graph; AG2 variant in multi_agents/ag2/main.py.

code.architecture: Library core gpt_researcher/: agent.py (GPTResearcher: conduct_research -> write_report, quick_search, cost tracking, source accessors) drives skills/ (researcher.py ResearchConductor plans sub-queries via actions/query_processing.py, runs retrievers per sub-query, scrapes and filters context; writer.py ReportGenerator; deep_research.py recursive breadth/depth research; browser.py scraper pool; curator.py; image_generator.py), actions/ (agent_creator.py role selection, retriever.py factory plus 'gpt_researcher.retrievers' entry-point plugins, markdown_processing.py add_references), retrievers/ (about 20 search backends; Tavily default via raw HTTP, plus duckduckgo, bing, brave, google, serper, serpapi, searx, exa, arxiv, openalex, semantic_scholar, pubmed_central, custom, mcp), scraper/ (bs default, selenium browser, nodriver, firecrawl, tavily_extract, pymupdf, arxiv), context/ (select.py CONTEXT_FILTER auto|jev|keyword|embeddings|none; jev_filter.py hosted TypeSafe API; lexical.py BM25 fallback; compression.py embeddings), document/ (local, online, Azure loaders), mcp/ (MCP client; LLM picks up to 3 tools; one tool-calling round with no allow/deny list), llm_provider/generic/base.py + utils/llm.py (LangChain provider factory; create_chat_completion with up to 10 attempts), utils/costs.py, utils/url_security.py (SSRF guard), utils/workers.py (the only 'worker' concept: scraper ThreadPoolExecutor + semaphore + global rate limiter), config/ (env > JSON > defaults). Service layer backend/ (server/app.py FastAPI REST + /ws, websocket_manager.py, report_store.py JSON-file store, chat/chat.py, report_type/ basic/detailed/deep, utils.py PDF/DOCX/MD export); main.py mounts it. multi_agents/ is a LangGraph ChiefEditorAgent pipeline (browser -> planner -> human review -> parallel researcher -> writer -> fact_checker -> visualizer -> publisher; bounded revision loops; compiled without a checkpointer, agents/orchestrator.py:5,159-171) with an AG2 variant. deep_agents/ is a LangChain deepagents chief-editor + researcher-subagent example whose tools wrap GPTResearcher (agent.py, tools.py) over a path-confined FilesystemBackend(virtual_mode=True) (agent.py:88), plus benchmark scripts and benchmark_results/. evals/ holds simple_evals (SimpleQA), quality_eval (citation faithfulness, source diversity/authority, unsupported-claim rate), hallucination_eval and context_filter. Also frontend/ (static + nextjs), docs/ (Docusaurus), terraform/ (maintainers' AWS deploy), and agent-packaging files .claude/, .codex-plugin/, .mcp.json, skills/. No sandbox, job queue, checkpoint store or coding agent exists in the tree.
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: PyPI distribution name gpt-researcher, version 0.16.0 in pyproject.toml:3,25 and setup.py:3, while the checked-out git tag is v3.7.0 (.git/packed-refs:2), so tag and package version disagree. Two build definitions coexist: a poetry-core backend (pyproject.toml:9-11; PEP 621 [project] with 140 dependencies) and a setuptools setup.py whose install_requires is requirements.txt minus lines containing selenium/webdriver/fastapi/uvicorn/jinja2/gpt-researcher/langgraph (setup.py:5-20,45); which of them produces the PyPI upload cannot be determined because no workflow publishes to PyPI. Container: Dockerfile (python:3.14-slim-bookworm, Chromium, Firefox, geckodriver, pip install of requirements.txt and multi_agents/requirements.txt, uvicorn CMD; Dockerfile:3-64), plus Dockerfile.fullstack and backend/Dockerfile (not read); docker-compose.yml builds locally (pull_policy: build, docker-compose.yml:3). Workflows in .github/workflows: build.yml builds an image on every push to master and pushes it to the maintainers' AWS ECR via an OIDC role, then dispatches deploy.yml (Terraform apply -auto-approve) (build.yml:4-7,51-91; deploy.yml:199-201). No workflow uploads to PyPI, Docker Hub or GitHub Releases; no checksums, signatures, SBOM or provenance attestations (search of .github for attest/sigstore/cosign/sha256/checksum/pypi/twine found nothing); no CHANGELOG or release-notes file in the tree.
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: pytest with pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode auto), pytest-timeout, pytest-forked (pyproject.toml:13-18,176-181). tests/ holds 135 pytest-collected test_*.py files (147 .py files in total, including conftest.py, __init__.py and about 10 hyphen-named or script-style files such as tests/test-your-llm.py, tests/report-types.py, tests/vector-store.py that python_files='test_*.py' does not match); subdirectories tests/backend, tests/chat, tests/retrievers, tests/skills. tests/conftest.py:21-36 implements an opt-in network kill-switch (GPTR_BLOCK_NETWORK=1, loopback allowed). Workflows: tests.yml ('Tests'; on pull_request and push to main/master; GPTR_BLOCK_NETWORK=1 at :14) runs three jobs: imports (py3.12/3.13/3.14; pip install -e .; imports the library, every gpt_researcher submodule and the ASGI app; :21-64), collect (pytest --collect-only; :69-83) and unit (needs both; py3.12-3.14; installs WeasyPrint system libs; warms the tiktoken cache; `pytest tests/ --forked --timeout=60 -p no:warnings`, deselecting test_researcher_logging.py, test_logging_output.py and test_mcp.py; :85-138) - a comment says the suite leaks global state across modules, hence --forked (:125-129) - so live/integration scripts are not run in CI. llm-costs.yml: tokentoll cost analysis on PRs (SHA-pinned action, continue-on-error for forks). plugin-quality-gate.yml: HOL Codex plugin scanner on PRs touching .codex-plugin/, skills/ or .mcp.json (min_score 80, fail_on_severity high). build.yml: Docker build + push to AWS ECR on push to master, then deploy.yml. docker-build.yml (named 'GPTR tests'): manual workflow_dispatch only, runs the docker-compose 'test' profile (tests/report-types.py, tests/vector-store.py; docker-compose.yml:47-62). No lint, formatter or type-check workflow or config (no ruff/flake8/mypy/pre-commit files found). .github/dependabot.yml: weekly pip and docker updates only (no npm).
code.dependencies: pyproject.toml: 140 entries in [project].dependencies (requires-python >=3.12; lower-bounded with >= only; includes langchain>=1.0.0, langgraph, langsmith, litellm, openai, mcp>=1.9.1,<2.0.0, fastapi, uvicorn, unstructured, pymupdf, weasyprint on non-win32); optional extras: test (4), requirements-txt (21; includes ag2, langchain-anthropic, langchain-google-genai, playwright, selenium, scrapy, firecrawl, exa_py), monocle (1); dependency-group dev (5 type stubs) (pyproject.toml:31-219). requirements.txt: 47 requirement lines (adds tavily-python, ddgs, google-genai, python-pptx, pandas, langchain-mcp-adapters, which pyproject.toml does not list). backend/requirements.txt: 21; multi_agents/requirements.txt: 7 lines (json5 duplicated); multi_agents/ag2/requirements.txt: 1; deep_agents/requirements.txt: 4 (deepagents>=0.7.8, langchain-openai, python-dotenv, tavily-python); evals/{simple_evals,quality_eval,hallucination_eval}/requirements.txt: 2 each. JavaScript: frontend/nextjs/package.json 25 dependencies + 34 devDependencies (includes next-plausible, react-ga4, @next/third-parties); docs/package.json 16; docs/npm/package.json 1 (ws); docs/discord-bot/package.json 6; multi_agents/package.json 1. No poetry.lock/uv.lock/Pipfile at the repo root. langchain-anthropic (needed for Claude) is only in the optional 'requirements-txt' extra and is otherwise pip-installed at runtime on first use (pyproject.toml:189; llm_provider/generic/base.py:160-164,407-425).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: report privately via GitHub private vulnerability reporting or email assaf.elovic@gmail.com, acknowledgement 'within a few business days' (SECURITY.md:3-12). Threat model: the backend is 'not a hardened, multi-tenant service' and ships without authentication by design; missing auth, SSRF/local-file access via user-supplied URLs, and RCE via user-supplied MCP command/args are declared out of scope (SECURITY.md:20-45). In scope: XSS/unsafe rendering of scraped or LLM content, DoS from untrusted content such as decompression bombs, reachable dependency vulnerabilities, path traversal/injection from normal research inputs (SECURITY.md:47-60). Security fixes only on the latest release on master (SECURITY.md:62-65).

claim_checks.claim: 'The agent produces detailed, factual, and unbiased research reports with citations' (README.md:27).
claim_checks.evidence: Citations are requested from the LLM by prompt (gpt_researcher/prompts.py:277-312: in-text markdown hyperlinks, a reference list, 'Do NOT cite sources that do not appear in the provided information'); DetailedReport appends a deterministic sorted list of all visited URLs (gpt_researcher/actions/markdown_processing.py:101-127; backend/report_type/detailed_report/detailed_report.py:200), i.e. visited, not necessarily cited, URLs. No pipeline step verifies that a cited URL supports a claim; the multi-agent FactCheckerAgent is one LLM pass over the draft (multi_agents/agents/fact_checker.py:20-32). Programmatic evidence accessors exist: get_source_urls() and get_research_sources() (gpt_researcher/agent.py:684-698,745-751), populated by gpt_researcher/skills/browser.py:58. The project's own FACT run verified 56.0% of citations (deep_agents/benchmark_results/drb/gptr-deepagent_fact_result.txt:3). README.md:356-359 says it does not aim to eliminate bias and README.md:354 says it is not a recommendation for academic/research papers.

claim_checks.claim: Deep Research: recursive tree-like exploration with configurable depth and breadth and concurrent processing (README.md:214-224).
claim_checks.evidence: gpt_researcher/skills/deep_research.py:250-263 reads breadth/depth/concurrency from config; :386-584 deep_research() generates `breadth` queries, runs one GPTResearcher per query under asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency) (:432-490), then recurses per result with breadth//2 (min 2) and depth-1 (:540-560), accumulating learnings, per-learning source-URL citations, visited URLs and context, trimmed to 25,000 words (:18,219-237,575). Defaults breadth 3 / depth 2 / concurrency 4 (gpt_researcher/config/variables/default.py:40-42). Failed branches are dropped and descent stops if all fail (deep_research.py:485-490,502-520). The skill has no wall-clock or cost ceiling.

claim_checks.claim: 'Takes ~5 minutes per deep research' and 'Costs ~$0.4 per research (using o3-mini on high reasoning effort)' (README.md:221-222; docs/docs/gpt-researcher/gptr/deep_research.md:5).
claim_checks.evidence: No measurement artifact for this figure exists in the repo. Cost tracking exists (gpt_researcher/agent.py:785-806; gpt_researcher/utils/costs.py:265-316) but defaults are now gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.4-mini rather than o3-mini (gpt_researcher/config/variables/default.py:8-10), and costs for models without a pricing-table entry use default per-token rates or token estimates (costs.py:257-262,306-316).

claim_checks.claim: 'Generate detailed reports exceeding 2,000 words' and 'Aggregate over 20 sources' (README.md:79-80).
claim_checks.evidence: Default TOTAL_WORDS is 1200 (gpt_researcher/config/variables/default.py:24); prompts ask for 'at least {total_words} words' (gpt_researcher/prompts.py:298,385,412) and report_generation.py:250-258 passes total_words=cfg.total_words for every report type including deep, overriding the deep-research prompt's own default of 2000 (prompts.py:424). Sources: MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS_PER_QUERY=5 (default.py:22), 3 planned sub-queries (MAX_ITERATIONS=3; default.py:26; gpt_researcher/actions/query_processing.py:113; prompts.py:246-248) plus the original query for non-subtopic reports (gpt_researcher/skills/researcher.py:369-371), so about 20 search results at most before URL de-duplication (plus an initial-results pass, researcher.py:387-391). risks: Scope gap versus an isolated, resumable worker: no sandbox or coding agent exists in the tree (only a Chrome --no-sandbox flag, gpt_researcher/scraper/browser/browser.py:122); the sole isolation is the example's path-confined deepagents FilesystemBackend (deep_agents/agent.py:88) and whatever container the operator runs. A WebSocket disconnect cancels the running task (backend/server/server_utils.py:406-408); background reports are in-process FastAPI BackgroundTasks with no job-status endpoint, only GET /report/{id} serving the DOCX once written (backend/server/app.py:174-179,371-381); LangGraph is compiled without a checkpointer (multi_agents/agents/orchestrator.py:5,159-171); the 'human_feedback' WebSocket command is a TODO stub (server_utils.py:189-192); persistence is a JSON report store and per-run JSON logs (backend/server/report_store.py:7-57; server_utils.py:41-87). No OpenAI Agents SDK / Claude Agent SDK / Codex SDK integration; the only harness SDKs are LangGraph, AG2 and LangChain deepagents.

Security posture: the backend has no authentication by design and takes client-supplied MCP command/args/env, source URLs and file uploads over REST/WebSocket (SECURITY.md:20-41; backend/server/server_utils.py:410-424; gpt_researcher/mcp/client.py:94-108); the maintainers classify RCE/SSRF through these as out of scope (SECURITY.md:37-41). MCP_ALLOWED_ROOT_PATHS is declared but never enforced (gpt_researcher/config/variables/default.py:47; config/config.py:55-61 only re-assigns it) and MCP tool use is bounded only by an LLM choosing at most 3 tools (gpt_researcher/mcp/tool_selector.py:37-55). docker-compose runs the API as root with restart: always, published on 8000 (docker-compose.yml:21-24) although the Dockerfile creates a non-root user (Dockerfile:51-59); default CORS allows credentials from https://app.gptr.dev (backend/server/app.py:99-120); the selenium Chrome scraper disables Chrome's sandbox (browser.py:122).

Runtime and build supply chain is loose: missing LLM-provider packages are pip-installed at runtime with `pip install -U` (gpt_researcher/llm_provider/generic/base.py:407-425) as are the tavily_extract/firecrawl scraper packages (gpt_researcher/scraper/scraper.py:160-192); the Dockerfile downloads geckodriver by URL without a checksum and installs unpinned requirements with --upgrade (Dockerfile:15-20,33-35); docker-build.yml curls a docker-compose 1.29.2 binary without verification (.github/workflows/docker-build.yml:41); there is no poetry.lock/uv.lock at the repo root and nearly all Python requirements are lower-bounded only; most CI actions are tag-pinned (e.g. hol-codex-plugin-scanner-action@v1, plugin-quality-gate.yml:16) with only tokentoll SHA-pinned (llm-costs.yml:21).

Release and licensing metadata are inconsistent and unautomated: git tag v3.7.0 vs package version 0.16.0 (pyproject.toml:3,25; setup.py:3); a poetry-core build (140 dependencies) and a setuptools setup.py (requirements.txt-derived, excluding fastapi/uvicorn/jinja2/langgraph) coexist with different dependency sets - e.g. pyproject.toml lists duckduckgo-search while the DuckDuckGo retriever imports ddgs and check_pkg only raises ImportError (gpt_researcher/retrievers/duckduckgo/duckduckgo.py:31-32; retrievers/utils.py:44-59), and langchain-mcp-adapters/tavily-python/google-genai appear only in requirements.txt:24,62; no workflow publishes to PyPI or produces checksums, signatures or attestations (build.yml pushes only to the maintainers' AWS ECR, :51-65); the published 0.16.0 release reportedly crashed on import on Python <3.14 (tests/test_package_imports.py:1-7; .github/workflows/tests.yml:18-20). License conflict: LICENSE and README say Apache-2.0 (LICENSE:1-3; README.md:354) while pyproject.toml:6,28, setup.py:33-35 and frontend/nextjs/package.json:102 say MIT; the LICENSE appendix keeps the unfilled 'Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]' placeholder (LICENSE:189) and there is no NOTICE file.

Model-support coupling: per-model behavior is a hard-coded list ending at gpt-5.5 and claude-opus-4-7 (gpt_researcher/llm_provider/generic/base.py:43-90), so an unlisted model ID (e.g. a GPT-6-series ID; the string appears in code nowhere, only docs config.md:25) gets temperature=0.4 and no reasoning_effort unless LLM_KWARGS overrides it (gpt_researcher/utils/llm.py:86-110); cost figures for unpriced models are estimates (utils/costs.py:257-262,306-316); Claude needs langchain-anthropic, available only via an optional extra or runtime pip install (pyproject.toml:189); docs still show claude-2.1 / claude-3-opus examples (docs/docs/gpt-researcher/llms/llms.md:170-180); the multi-agent path takes its provider from SMART_LLM but its model name from STRATEGIC_LLM/task.json, so mixed-provider setups can mismatch (multi_agents/main.py:58-65; multi_agents/agents/utils/llms.py:20-26).

Evidence quality for evaluation use: citations are prompt-driven and not verified in the pipeline (gpt_researcher/prompts.py:277-312; multi_agents/agents/fact_checker.py:20-32); the project's own FACT run verified 56.0% of citations (deep_agents/benchmark_results/drb/gptr-deepagent_fact_result.txt:3); get_source_urls() returns visited URLs, not cited ones (gpt_researcher/agent.py:745-751); a DuckDuckGo bug once shipped reports with zero verifiable citations (gpt_researcher/retrievers/duckduckgo/duckduckgo.py:5-19); POST /report/ omits raw research_sources from its response (backend/server/app.py:356-360); the README itself disclaims suitability for academic/research papers and bias elimination (README.md:354-359); the repo's hallucination-eval artifact has n=2 and a record flagged is_hallucination: true whose reasoning says no hallucination was found (evals/hallucination_eval/results/aggregate_results.json:2-19).

All published performance numbers are first-party, small-sample and LLM-judged: DeepResearch Bench on 10 tasks with a locally patched harness using OpenAI judges instead of the stock Gemini judge (deep_agents/BENCHMARK.md:7-9,25-29,119-121); the benchmarked agent differs from the shipped example (deep_agents/benchmark.py:114-121 vs deep_agents/agent.py:63-89); per-task wins are not in the tracked artifacts; SimpleQA 'parity' compares two different runs while earlier runs scored lower for GPT Researcher (deep_agents/benchmark_results/simpleqa_2026-07-04_13-07-09_n30.json:364; simpleqa_2026-07-04_13-55-24_n30.json:17); the head-to-head shows the baseline ahead on citation_quality 6-2 and factual_grounding 5-3 (reports_2026-07-04_14-33-21_n8.json:16-25); the context-filter study uses 28 questions and one judge family (evals/context_filter/README.md:145-150). Third-party egress in optional parts: the NextJS UI loads Plausible and Google Analytics components (frontend/nextjs/app/layout.tsx:65-66); setting TYPESAFE_API_KEY sends each scraped ~1,000-character chunk plus the question to api.typesafe.ai (gpt_researcher/context/jev_filter.py:32,84-101,144); runners auto-enable LangSmith tracing when LANGCHAIN_API_KEY is set (multi_agents/main.py:42-44; deep_agents/main.py:12-13).
